hypothesis: For wide grids, statically work-sharing each row as four independent segmented-prefix chunks can parallelize the dense DP while a constant-size carry scan preserves values across chunk boundaries. A sequential path avoids OpenMP synchronization overhead on smaller grids, and storing obstacles by row reduces mask storage from O(n²) to O(n + m).
notes: Source-only experiment for the supplied four-core ARM64/GCC target. Correctness relies on the row recurrence and exact carry propagation; no execution or benchmark was performed. OpenMP directives provide parallel execution when the build enables OpenMP and remain semantically safe if directives are ignored.
transformations: Replace the n-by-n blocked-cell mask with sorted blocked-column lists per row, using O(n + m) obstacle storage.

Keep the row dependency sequential and implement each wide row as four statically scheduled local segmented prefix scans, followed by a serial scan of chunk summaries and parallel carry correction before the next row.
Use a sequential row scan below a fixed grid-size threshold to avoid parallel-team and synchronization overhead for small workloads.
